guard: a stored row's allowDmOwners survives the resolver into the mint, absent stays absent and empty stays empty, and no child may out-reach its spawner's DM list while an unscoped spawner constrains nothing
why: This config exists because the CORE suite for this feature could not see any of the code below.
Measured, not argued: an unconditional throw at the top of implementations/auth/src/ledger.ts
left `pnpm smoke:dm-scope:auth` reporting 12 passed, 0 failed, rc=0. It imports core and never
loads the auth package at all. So a mutant aimed at the carry there was UNREACHABLE, not
survived — and an unreachable mutant is not a weak test, it is no test. E0 below makes that
check permanent for THIS suite, because a coverage claim that was true when written is exactly
the kind that rots silently: the day someone refactors the imports, E0 goes green and says so.
E0 IS THE INSTRUMENT CONTROL AND MUST RUN FIRST. Every verdict under it is void if it fails:
a mutation proves the suite depends on the code only once the file is known to be loaded.
E1/E2 are the carry. `allowDmOwners` is the NEWEST of the three ACL fields, so its failure mode
was never a wrong line but a MISSING one — a resolver carrying read and post and omitting DM
reverts that principal to the historical wildcard, turning a stored 'no DM at all' into 'DM
anyone' with core byte-unchanged. E2 is the ordinary `?.length` empty-guard idiom, which is the
shape a hand-written carry actually acquires and which leaves the ABSENT case correct.
E3/E4/E5 are delegation. E3 deletes the envelope check entirely. E4 is subtler and is the one a
reviewer would wave through: it drops only the ABSENT-child default, so a child that OMITS the
field slips past while every explicit widening is still caught — and omission is the widest ask
there is. E5 goes the other way and breaks upgrade safety, refusing children of an unscoped
parent; every security cell stays green under it and only the upgrade-direction cells object.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite imports ../src/ledger.js directly and CALLS those functions, so a
mutation to that file is a mutation to the code under test. Its structural cells additionally
read the same file from disk; those alone could pass without loading it, which is precisely why
the behavioural cells and E0 carry the weight.

mutations.name: E0 LOAD PROOF — the suite must actually load ledger.ts
mutations.replace:
throw new Error("LOAD PROBE: ledger.ts was imported");
export interface ActorRow {
mutations.note: If this does NOT kill the suite, every other verdict in this file is meaningless: the mutated file was never loaded. This is the exact check that reclassified the core suite's E5 from 'survived' to 'unreachable'. Carries its own completionMarker because a load proof necessarily dies BEFORE the suite's normal end marker — grading it against that marker would score the proof as unfinished rather than as the control it is.

mutations.name: E1 the carry drops the field entirely
mutations.expectRed: a SCOPED row's list reaches the mint opts
mutations.cell: a SCOPED row's list reaches the mint opts
mutations.note: The whole-feature revert: every principal silently returns to the historical wildcard. Core is byte-unchanged, so no core cell moves.

mutations.name: E2 the `?.length` empty-guard idiom in the carry
mutations.expectRed: an EMPTY row carries [] through — it is NOT dropped as falsy
mutations.cell: an EMPTY row carries [] through — it is NOT dropped as falsy
mutations.note: Leaves ABSENT correct, so the upgrade-path cells stay green; only a stored EMPTY row is silently re-widened to DM-anyone. The likeliest hand-written regression on this line.

mutations.name: E3 delegation forgets the field exists
mutations.expectRed: a child adding an owner the parent lacks is REFUSED
mutations.cell: a child adding an owner the parent lacks is REFUSED
mutations.note: The pre-fix state: any agent holding `spawn` escapes its own DM policy in one hop.

mutations.name: E4 the ABSENT-CHILD default is dropped
mutations.expectRed: a child that OMITS the field under a scoped parent is REFUSED (absent means "*")
mutations.cell: a child that OMITS the field under a scoped parent is REFUSED (absent means "*")
mutations.note: Every EXPLICIT widening is still caught, so E3's cell stays green. Only omission slips through — and omission is the widest ask there is, while reading in a diff as though it asks for nothing.

mutations.name: E5 the ABSENT-PARENT default is dropped (upgrade safety)
mutations.expectRed: a child of an ABSENT-list parent may hold any list
mutations.cell: a child of an ABSENT-list parent may hold any list
mutations.note: Every security cell stays green — this mutant only REFUSES more. It would break every existing deployment's spawns on upgrade, which is the exact failure the default-allow design exists to prevent, and only an upgrade-direction cell can see it.
